text: 8 “What’s on your radar, Brian?” Nick asked. “Anything unusual? Anything at all?” “No,” Brian said. “It says the world is down there, and that’s all it says. We’re—” “Wait,” Nick said. His voice had a tight, strangled sound, as if his throat had closed down to a bare pinhole. “Climb back up. Let’s think this over. Wait for the clouds to break—” “Not enough time and not enough fuel.” Brian’s eyes were locked on his instruments. The plane began to bounce again. He made the corrections automatically. “Hang on. We’re going in.” He pushed the wheel forward. The altimeter needle began to move more swiftly beneath its glass circle. And Flight 29 slid into the clouds. For a moment its tail protruded, cutting through the fluffy surface like the fin of a shark. A moment later that was also gone and the sky was empty... as if no plane had ever been there at all.
